PCI DSS v4 doesn’t require setting org-level risk objectives. It focuses on targeted risk analyses to tune specific controls and frequencies, or risk-based ranking for vulnerability remediation. Those are implementation-level and don’t directly produce the CSF outcome of agreed risk management objectives

GV.RM-03 requires that cybersecurity risk activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management (ERM). PCI DSS v4 does not require ERM integration; it prescribes control implementation for the cardholder data environment. PCI’s “risk-based” elements (e.g., targeted risk analyses, risk-based frequencies, vulnerability risk ranking) are implementation-level and within PCI scope, not enterprise-level governance. PCI does not establish risk appetite/tolerance, ERM roles, enterprise risk registers, portfolio aggregation, or formal ERM reporting/escalation. Where overlap exists (e.g., internal reviews/exec communication), it is illustrative or precedes ERM inclusion rather than being integral to achieving it. Therefore these mappings are “example of” only - useful inputs that an organization may feed into ERM, but not required by PCI and not sufficient to satisfy GV.RM-03 on their own.

GV.RM-04 is about establishing and communicating strategic risk-response options (accept/avoid/mitigate/transfer) and related criteria/delegations across the enterprise. PCI DSS v4 focuses on incident response procedures and operational risk-based tuning within the CDE, not organization-wide risk-treatment strategy. As such, 12.10.x shows examples of response execution in the incident domain rather than defining enterprise risk-response strategy - hence the lower strength.
